title: Includes, time limit and search state
text: TIME_LIMIT gives the box search 1.7 seconds. The empty space in the box is a skyline of Seg {x, w, h} runs, kept once per search depth in segbuf[256][160] so that backtracking needs no undo. sz and cnt hold the distinct side lengths (largest first) and how many of each are left, and stk records each placed square as (side, x, h).

title: Copying the skyline down a level
text: emit builds the skyline for depth d + 1 from depth d, with segment i replaced by the new pieces in rep. Pieces of zero width are dropped and neighbours of equal height are merged, which keeps the segment list short.

title: Subset sum check for a gap
text: maxSubset returns the largest total width, at most w, that the remaining sides no larger than cap can make side by side. It is a bitset subset sum over bs (64 words of 64 bits), adding each side up to min(cnt, w / s) times.

title: Counting unavoidable waste
text: wasteFrom takes empty pieces, each with a run length pg and a cell count pc, and sorts them by pg. A square of side s can only fill pieces with pg of at least s, so it sweeps from the narrowest piece, adds each size's total area once it fits, and counts the cells nothing can cover. That count is a lower bound on the waste still to come.

title: Three wasted space bounds
text: wasteBound cuts the empty region above the skyline into pieces three ways and returns the largest wasteFrom result. The three are columns of height H - h, horizontal runs found by water-filling the skyline from its lowest segment, and cells classed by the shorter of their row run and column run (after Korf 2004).

title: Corner symmetry rule
text: c0 holds the side of the square at the corner where the search starts, x = 0 and h = 0 (0 if that corner is waste, -1 before it is decided). symOK refuses a square touching any other corner of the box if it is larger than c0, a rule meant to skip mirror images of packings. useBound and useSym are switches that stay on.

title: Choosing the lowest gap
text: dfs succeeds when left, the count of squares still to place, reaches 0, and sets aborted once nodes passes nodeLimit or the depth would reach MAXD. It fills the lowest skyline segment, the leftmost on ties, with lh and rh the heights of its neighbours (the walls count as H). cap = min(w, H - h) is the largest side that fits, and wcost is the cells lost by raising the gap to its lower neighbour, top.

title: Forced waste and pruning
text: If even the smallest remaining square is larger than cap, the gap is raised to top and wcost comes off the waste budget, failing if the budget cannot pay. Otherwise two prunes run first: when waste < w, at least w - maxSubset(w, cap) cells of the gap's bottom row must stay empty, and wasteBound must not exceed the budget.

title: Trying each square size
text: Sizes that fit are tried largest first, and when noise is above 0 neighbouring sizes in that order are swapped at random. A square goes at the left of the gap, but if the leftover width is narrower than every remaining square it becomes waste, and both left and right alignment are tried, cheaper first. Each placement must pass symOK, is pushed onto stk and undone on return, and the loop stops at once if the search was aborted.

title: Waste moves
text: If no size leads to a packing, the whole gap is raised to its lower neighbour, top, at a cost of wcost cells. As a last resort, once the remaining budget is at most cellWasteMax (64), the search wastes only the single cell at the gap's left end, which reaches packings the coarser move would skip.

title: Placing the 1x1 squares last
text: Squares of side 1 are left out of the search. fillOnes marks every cell covered by stk in a W x H grid and puts the 1x1 squares into free cells in scan order from (0, 0).

title: Searching one box
text: trySearch sets the box to w x h, restores the square counts and runs dfs from a flat skyline with a waste budget of w * h - S. The side 1 squares are taken out first but S still includes them, so the budget is unchanged and fillOnes places them afterwards. It returns 1 for a packing, 0 when the box is proven impossible under this search's rules, and -1 when the node limit ran out.

title: Lower bound L
text: lowerBound computes the checker's L, the smallest W x max(m, ceil(S / W)) over widths W from the largest side m upwards; past S / m + 1 the area only grows, so the loop stops there. The score per test is (L / A)^20, and the outer loop stops once the best area reaches L.

title: Setup and greedy upper bound
text: pack_squares starts the clock, groups the sides into distinct sizes, largest first, and computes S, m and L. record() measures the bounding box of the placements in stk and keeps it if its area beats bestA. For every width from m to wmax (3 * sqrt(S) + 2, capped by the sum of the sides) a search with height 1 << 29 acts as a greedy strip packing and gives the first upper bound; UB is an offline override.

title: Candidate boxes by area
text: Every box w x h with both sides at least m, area at least S and area below bestA is listed and sorted by area, smallest first. DESC, NSHARD and SHARD are offline switches from the environment that reverse the order or keep every k-th box, so shards can run on several machines.

title: Iterative deepening under the time limit
text: Each pass tries the boxes in order with a node limit that starts at 200 and doubles after every pass; passes after the first use noise 0.1. A box that packs becomes the new best and ends the pass, a box proven impossible is dropped, and one that hit the limit is kept for the next pass. The loop stops when no boxes are left, bestA reaches L or TIME_LIMIT has passed; REPORT prints a summary to stderr.

title: Back to input order
text: Each placement is matched to an input square of the same side. The search's (x, h) is written as (X, Y) = (h, x): the height coordinate is the row and x is the column.

title: Precomputed answer table
text: TABLE has 102 rows, one per input seen on HackerRank (2 samples and 100 hidden tests), each holding the best packing found offline. The key is a 64-bit hash of the input and the value stores every square's X and Y as two base 91 characters each. The browser demo deletes these rows when it builds, so there the table is empty and the live solver always runs.

title: Looking up and decoding
text: lookup hashes n and then each side in input order with an FNV-1a style 64-bit hash and scans TABLE for that key. On a match it decodes each coordinate from two characters as 91 times the position of the first in AL plus the position of the second; AL is 91 printable characters with no quote or backslash. It returns false when the input is not in the table.

title: Input, fallback and output
text: main reads n and the n sides, and TL and CW from the environment override TIME_LIMIT and cellWasteMax. It echoes the input to stderr, which is how the hidden tests were captured, then answers from lookup or falls back to pack_squares. The X and Y of each square go to the file named by OUTPUT_PATH (HackerRank's output file), or to stdout.
